title: Container sidecar dies silently on firewall-init failure (dnsmasq port 53): no surfacing, no respawn
description: Container mode. cam run spawns the sidecar (background supervisor, the sole driver of plan/implement/review/ship and the meta_loop=auto driver). At boot the sidecar runs the container firewall init (dnsmasq on port 53). Observed 2026-07-06 20:36: init failed with 'dnsmasq: failed to create listening socket for port 53: Address already in use' (a stale cam-worker container from an earlier session held port 53), the sidecar logged '[cam] container firewall init failed - no worker will be dispatched' and EXITED, becoming a zombie. Three compounding gaps: (1) no surfacing: the failure only lands in .claude/cam-supervisor.log; the orchestrator boot reads no marker (unlike .cam-ship-stalled.json / .cam-plan-escalated.json), so a subsequent cam plan / meta-loop phase:planning signal is written and silently never consumed (cam plan liveness gate checks the orchestrator pane, not the sidecar pid, so it exits 0 into a hang). (2) no respawn: nothing restarts a dead sidecar - only cam run-creates-session spawns it, and orch-recycle-watch only watches the orchestrator. Recovery today requires a full operator ceremony (cam stop + docker rm -f cam-worker + cam run). (3) no fail-safe on the collision: firewall init does not detect/reap a stale cam-worker container (or an existing dnsmasq) holding port 53 before binding, so a leftover container from a prior session hard-wedges the next session. Durable fixes: sidecar writes a durable escalation marker on firewall-init failure that the orchestrator surfaces at boot (mirror the ship-stalled/plan-escalated pattern); a sidecar-liveness watcher (parallel to orch-recycle-watch) that respawns or surfaces a dead sidecar; and firewall init that reaps a stale container/dnsmasq on the port-53 collision and retries fail-closed. Ties CAM-192 (image staleness), CAM-201 (container/CI parity + preflight fail-closed), CAM-180 (rebuild ceremony).

acceptanceCriteria: Story 1 (surfacing): the FirewallError arm at src/commands/sidecar.ts:2410-2415 writes a durable .cam-sidecar-stalled.json marker ({ reason:'firewall-init-failed', detail, writtenAt }) via a never-throw write/read/remove helper module mirroring src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts. The orchestrator boot-read adds this marker to the three it already surfaces (ship-stalled, plan-escalated, plan-preflight-failed) and prints an opening blocker line '⚠ sidecar stalled: <reason> — <detail>'. The marker is removed on the next healthy sidecar bring-up (mirroring the plan-escalated remove-on-converge lifecycle).

Story 2 (respawn/watch): a new sidecar-liveness watcher command mirrors src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts (poll loop + injectable pid-resolve/kill seams), discovers the sidecar via .cam-sidecar.pid plus a new composite sidecarAlive() in src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts, and on a dead sidecar attempts a bounded respawn (N attempts with backoff); on exhaustion it writes the shared .cam-sidecar-stalled.json marker ({ reason:'sidecar-died' }) and stops respawning (escalate, never hot-loop). Spawn wiring in src/commands/run.ts (alongside orch-recycle-watch) and cleanup in stop.ts.

Story 3 (gate): cam plan / cam next / cam ship liveness gates check sidecarAlive() in addition to the orchestrator pane; when the sidecar is dead the command refuses with a clear error instead of writing a phase:planning / active:true / phase:shipping signal into the void (fixing the silent hang; host-relevant, not container-only).

Story 4 (port-53 fail-safe): stop.ts tears down the cam-worker container at session exit (docker rm -f) so no stale running container with a stale dnsmasq is inherited by the next session; and .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh detects a port-53 collision, reaps the dnsmasq actually holding the port (not only the one in /var/run/dnsmasq-cam.pid) plus one retry, and fails closed if still blocked.

All container-gated behavior (stories 1, 2, 4) is a no-op when worker_isolation != 'container'; story 3's sidecarAlive gate applies in host mode too. Because this repo runs worker_isolation='host', these paths are validated by tests, not by a live run (the live container ceremony is CAM-175, still open).
spec.scope: Close the three compounding gaps that let the container-mode sidecar die silently on firewall-init failure (dnsmasq port 53 already in use from a stale cam-worker container of a prior session), plus the liveness-gate bug that makes the resulting hang silent. One PRD, four independent stories: (1) durable .cam-sidecar-stalled.json marker surfaced at orchestrator boot; (2) a sidecar-liveness watcher (bounded respawn then surface, mirroring orch-recycle-watch) with a new sidecarAlive() composite; (3) cam plan/next/ship gates check sidecarAlive so a dead sidecar refuses the signal-write rather than orphaning it (host-relevant); (4) root-cause container teardown at session exit + a port-53 reap-and-retry in init-firewall.sh. Fix 4 alone prevents THIS wedge; fixes 1/2/3 are defense-in-depth for ANY silent sidecar death. Cross-refs: CAM-192/201/180 shipped; CAM-175 (live-validation ceremony) still open.
gotchas: This repo is worker_isolation='host', so stories 1/2/4 are inert locally and can only be validated by tests, never by a live run; the live container run is the still-open CAM-175 ceremony. Do not claim live validation of the container paths.

Container gating: readWorkerIsolation (src/config/models.ts:300-315) fail-closes to 'host'; the boot guard (sidecar.ts:2403-2404) and firewall/config seams are no-ops in host mode. Story 3's gate must work in BOTH modes (the orphaned-signal hang is isolation-agnostic).

The single shared marker .cam-sidecar-stalled.json is written by two producers (the firewall arm and the watcher) with a structured reason field; do not create two separate marker files. Surfacing it touches templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md (+ embedded copy + templates/.gitignore) and requires bun run embed-vendor + embed-vendor:check.

The watcher must not respawn a sidecar that keeps dying on a deterministic firewall failure (hot-loop): the bound + surface-on-exhaustion is the guard, mirroring the orchestrator wrapper's respawn cap.

Root cause of the collision: stop.ts today cleans only tmux/markers, never the container (stop.ts:465-472), and ensure-container reuses a running cam-worker (ensure-container.ts:335-337), inheriting its stale dnsmasq. Tearing the container down at exit means the next session restarts (fast) or rebuilds (only if image-stale) via the existing absent->build path.

sidecarAlive() is new: .cam-sidecar.pid exists (sidecar-pid.ts:18, readSidecarPid :37, sidecarPidAlive :65) but there is no composite sidecarAlive() (only watcherAlive() at :153-157); story 2 adds it and story 3 consumes it.
